items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to preferred source status
for entities that provide employment to certain persons
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7578

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to preferred source
status for entities that provide employment to certain persons

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation will update the preferred source statute by eliminating
outdated language, clarifies definitions, expanding thresholds for inte-
grated employment, increasing the contract amount eligible for expedited
review.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Amends state finance law, section 162 by:

-Removes outdated language including "workshops" and severely" disabled

-Requires nonprofit partner contracts to have a minimum of 50%

employment of disabled individuals to receive preferred source statuts,
which mirrors the business/corporate partner requirement

-Raises the threshold for commissioner review of purchases from $50,000
to $250,000

-Removes language related to a pilot program, which is now permanent

-Clarifies which entities are required to use preferred source by defin-
ing political subdivision

-Expands the preferred source program to workforce development grants

Section 2. Effective Date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The preferred source requirements were enacted over forty-five years ago
with minimal changes being made since 1995. This legislation is intended
to provide some much-needed modernization to better reflect how procure-
ment is effectuated in the twenty-first century. Archaic terms such as
workshop and severely disabled are used throughout showing a lack of
connection to today's world.

The preferred source program currently relies on multiple guidance docu-
ments from its overseeing agency and this legislation seeks to codify
those practices for ease of use and transparency. The program is also
hampered by a low discretionary purchasing threshold that is at least
$200,000 lower than other comparable thresholds in other parts of State
Law.

Finally, the use of corporate partners has been in place for over a
decade and its reference as a pilot program in the current statute
belies the reality that the pilot was sun setted many years ago.  Corpo-
rate partnering provides significant competitive integrated employment
opportunities.
Additionally, the requirement for utilizing preferred sources should be
expanded to those receiving workforce development grants to increase
opportunities for disabled workers across the State. If you are receiv-
ing significant workforce development dollars from the State there is no
reason to leave these underserved communities out of your supply chain
diversification goals. Doing so cuts across the very notion of why the
State decided to create a preferred source program all those years ago.
Workforce development grants have MWBE requirements but currently do not
have preferred source requirements.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

There are no fiscal impacts to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Effective immediately.

AN ACT to amend the state finance law, in relation to preferred source status

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7578B

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to preferred source
status for entities that provide employment to certain persons; and
providing for the repeal of certain provisions upon the expiration ther-
eof

 
PURPOSE:

To modernize the preferred source statute.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one modernizes multiple terms within the preferred source stat-
ute including references to "workshops" and "severely" disabled.

It also creates new thresholds for what percentage of a preferred source
contract must be performed by disabled, or otherwise qualified, persons
to receive preferred source status. The threshold for discretionary
spending is increased and outdated reporting requirements are removed.

Finally, it clarifies what entities are captured by the statute and
expands when the program would be triggered. Section two provides for an
immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The preferred source requirements contained within State Finance Law §
162 were enacted over forty-five years ago with minimal changes being
made since 1995.

This legislation is intended to provide some much-need ed modernization
to better reflect how procurement is effectuated in the twenty-first
century. Archaic terms such as workshop and severely disabled are used
throughout showing a lack of connection to today's world.

The preferred source program currently relies on multiple guidance docu-
ments from its overseeing agency and this legislation seeks to codify
those practices for ease of use and transparency. The program is also
hampered by a low discretionary purchasing threshold that is at least
$200,000 lower than other comparable thresholds in other parts of State
Law.

Finally, the use of corporate partners has been in place for over a
decade and its reference as a pilot program in the current statute
belies the reality that the pilot was sun settled many years ago.
Corporate partnering provides significant competitive integrated employ-
ment opportunities. Additionally, the requirement for utilizing
preferred sources should be expanded to those receiving workforce devel-
opment grants to increase opportunities for disabled workers across the
State.

If you are receiving significant workforce development dollars from the
State there is no reason to leave these underserved communities out of
your supply chain diversification goals. Doing so cuts across the very

notion of why the State decided to create a preferred source program all
those years ago.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

There are no fiscal impacts to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided that section one of
this act shall expire and be deemed repealed three years after such
effective date and this act shall not apply to any contracts or requests
for proposals issued by government entities before such date.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 17 Chapter 565
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 7578-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the state finance law, in relation to preferred
        source status for entities that provide  employment  to  certain
        persons"
 
    APPROVED
 
  The  preferred  source  requirements  are  a vital tool to provide job
support to people with disabilities and  the  visually  impaired.  These
requirements,  contained  within  State  Finance  Law  Section 162, were
enacted over forty-five years ago with minimal changes being made  since
1995.
 
  This legislation modernizes the statute to better reflect how procure-
ment  is  effectuated,  replaces  outdated  terminology  and makes other
necessary technical amendments. The legislation also codifies  a  number
of  existing practices that currently exist in agency guidance. Finally,
the legislation increases  the  discretionary  purchasing  threshold  to
ensure  commissioner  review  happens  for  contracts valued at over one
hundred thousand dollars.
 
  This legislation required a technical amendment to ensure  the  legis-
lation  is applicable to commodities produced by preferred source member
agencies serving people who  are  visually  impaired  or  blind.  Having
agreed  to those changes with the Legislature, I am pleased to sign this
bill into law.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
